A place or office is not a legal branch.
Workplace designation and allocation are effective-dated.

model.name: Facility
model.purpose: Provide the governed, format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, compose, operate, evidence and hand over a built facility as a managed aggregation of buildings, structures, systems and grounds.
model.scope_statement: A Facility is a bounded, operationally managed built entity that is planned, constructed, operated, maintained and eventually decommissioned as a unit under identified custody, and that aggregates one or more buildings, structures, engineered systems and associated grounds. The model covers the facility as (a) an identifiable real-world entity with registry standing, (b) an aggregation root over contained buildings and systems, and (c) an object of regulatory, financial, security and information governance. It deliberately excludes the internals of contained models (Building, Space, Equipment) and the land-tenure semantics of the containing Site.
in_scope: Facility identity, naming, reference designation and cross-registry keys
Functional, occupancy and code classification of the facility as an operating whole
Geospatial extent, georeference and jurisdictional location of the facility boundary
Containment by Site and decomposition into facility parts, buildings and structures
Facility-level engineered systems and linkage to the component asset register
Lifecycle phase, operational status, milestone events and record versioning
Condition, service life, deferred maintenance and criticality at facility level
Ownership, custody, legal interest, operator and facility-management accountability
Regulatory programme interests, permits, statutory inspections and nonconformities
Security level, protective posture and information disclosure constraints
Capacity, occupancy, utilisation and resource performance benchmarking
Asset information requirements, provenance, retention and standards alignment
out_of_scope: Land parcel tenure, cadastral boundaries and site acquisition (Site model WM-BLT-008)
Internal building fabric, storeys, structural systems and envelope (Building model WM-BLT-001)
Room and space geometry, occupancy assignment and wayfinding (Space model)
Component-level equipment records, serial numbers, warranties and spares (Equipment/Asset-item model)
Legal-entity attributes of owners, operators and regulators (Organization/Party model)
The permit or licence instrument itself, including its issuance workflow (Authorization model)
Postal address normalisation and address-point registry semantics (Address model)
Work-order execution, labour, scheduling and cost postings (Work Management model)
Financial valuation, depreciation and capital accounting (Financial Asset model)
Linear network topology of utilities and transport corridors beyond the facility boundary (Network/Utility model)
Individual person records, credentials and access-card issuance (Identity/Access model)
Construction project delivery, contracts and programme management (Project model)

boundary_notes.distinction: Site is the georeferenced land locus with tenure and parcel semantics; Facility is the operating unit placed on or spanning one or more sites. IFC keeps IfcSite and IfcFacility as distinct spatial structure elements and allows IfcFacility to be aggregated directly to IfcProject when no site information exists, so Site containment is normal but not universal.

Facility aggregates buildings and structures; Building holds fabric, storeys and envelope. This inverts the IFC type hierarchy, where IfcBuilding is a subtype of IfcFacility rather than its part. The registry CONTAINS relation is retained as an operational aggregation, and IFC subtyping is recorded as an alignment conflict rather than a conformance claim.

Facility stops at facility parts and building membership; interior spatial subdivision (IfcSpace, COBie Space and Zone, CityGML rooms) belongs to the Space model. Facility records only aggregate space counts and area totals.

Facility records facility-level systems and a pointer to the asset register with coverage and completeness measures; individual component identity, type data and maintenance history belong to the Equipment model (COBie Type and Component).

Facility references owner, custodian, demand organisation and service provider by identifier and role, with validity dates; it does not model legal-entity registration, corporate hierarchy or contracting capacity.

Facility carries regulatory programme interests, programme identifiers and permit references with validity windows; the permit instrument, its conditions text and issuance workflow belong to the Authorization model. EPA FRS models this as environmental interest types linked to a facility Registry ID.
Facility holds address references and administrative unit codes needed for reporting and emergency response; address parsing, normalisation and address-point authority belong to the Address model.

Facility is the object of management, not the management system. FM policy, objectives, competence and audit of the FM management system belong to a separate management-system model; Facility retains only the accountability links and service scope.

selectedFindings.name: Building-code occupancy and hazard classification
selectedFindings.description: The regulatory occupancy groups assigned under the applicable building code edition, construction type, mixed-occupancy treatment and the highest hazard class present. This classification is legally consequential and is asserted by an authority having jurisdiction, unlike operational typologies.

selectedFindings.name: Facility geometry, georeference and level of detail
selectedFindings.description: The representative point and boundary geometry of the facility, the coordinate reference system and vertical datum, positional accuracy, and the level of detail at which geometry is held. CityGML supplies LoD semantics, INSPIRE supplies accuracy and elevation reference expectations, and IFC supplies relative placement against site or parent facility.

selectedFindings.name: Addressing and jurisdictional placement
selectedFindings.description: Addresses used for postal, service, regulatory and emergency purposes, plus the administrative and jurisdictional units the facility falls within, including cases where it straddles a boundary. Address values are references into a sibling Address model; only role, authority and jurisdiction assignment are held here.

selectedFindings.name: Site containment and boundary exclusivity
selectedFindings.description: The typed edge from the containing Site to this Facility, whether that containment is exclusive, whether the facility spans multiple sites or parcels, and how facility identity survives site subdivision or amalgamation. IFC permits a facility with no site at all, so containment must be modelled as conditional.

selectedFindings.name: Facility part decomposition and building membership
selectedFindings.description: How the facility breaks down into parts and which buildings or structures are members over which periods. IFC requires an explicit usage convention for each facility part, and permits a facility to be part of a facility part, which allows longitudinal or regional division of larger facilities.

selectedFindings.name: Lifecycle phase, operational status and milestone events
selectedFindings.description: The facility's position in the ISO 15686-1 life cycle (initiation, project definition, design, construction, commissioning, operation, maintenance, refurbishment, replacement, deconstruction and disposal), its current operational status, and the milestone events that changed either. INSPIRE supplies a construction-condition code list and ISO 19650-3 supplies operational trigger events that require an information exchange.

selectedFindings.name: Operator and facility-management accountability
selectedFindings.description: The chain from demand organisation to facility-management service provider, the scope of services delegated, the governing agreement, and the named accountable person for statutory duties. ISO 41011 makes the demand-organisation and service-provider distinction the core of facility-management vocabulary.

selectedFindings.name: Occupancy authorization and authority having jurisdiction
selectedFindings.description: Under IBC 111.1, a building or structure shall not be used or occupied, and a change of occupancy shall not be made, until the building official has issued a certificate of occupancy. Certificates that presume authority to violate the code are not valid. Work exempt from permit may be excepted. This rule is building-code-centric; roads, railways and some civil facilities are authorized by other AHJs. A CO authorizes occupancy under the building code; it does not by itself satisfy ongoing fire-code, elevator or environmental program duties. Phased projects may require occupancy authorization before occupying portions.

selectedFindings.name: Information disclosure and access constraints
selectedFindings.description: Which facility attributes may be published, which must be withheld or generalised, on what legal basis, who may grant exceptions, and what must be logged. Federal real-property publication law expressly authorises excluding assets for national-security reasons and under freedom-of-information exemptions, establishing that facility inventories are not uniformly public.

selectedFindings.name: Area, capacity, occupancy and utilisation
selectedFindings.description: Area measures under a declared measurement standard, design capacity, occupant population by category, operating schedule and derived utilisation. Gross floor area and operating-hours style use details are the mandatory inputs to benchmarking, while facility population and size are two of the five security-level determination factors.

selectedFindings.name: Criticality, hazard exposure and operational continuity
selectedFindings.description: The facility's criticality or mission-dependency rating and the method behind it, the natural and human-caused hazards it is exposed to, redundancy and alternate-facility arrangements, and when continuity plans were last exercised. Criticality drives both asset-management investment prioritisation and the mission-criticality factor in security-level determination.

composition.purpose: Bind the facility to its containing site or sites for georeference, tenure context and portfolio rollup, while leaving parcel and land-tenure semantics in the Site model. Modelled as conditional because a facility may be the outermost spatial container.
Aggregate the buildings and structures that constitute the facility, with membership validity and exclusivity, delegating fabric, storeys and envelope to the Building model.
Reference interior spaces and zones for area totals, service relationships and occupancy without duplicating space geometry or assignment.
Link the facility to component-level asset records via a declared linkage key, with register coverage and inventory recency held here and item detail held there.
Resolve owner, custodian, demand organisation, service provider, regulator and assessor roles to governed party identifiers with validity windows.
Attach permits, licences and programme authorisations to the facility by reference, keeping instrument text, conditions and issuance workflow in the Authorization model.
Resolve role-tagged addresses and administrative units without embedding address parsing or address-point authority.
Resolve work orders, jobs and resources back to facility and system so that maintenance backlog and history are computable without duplicating execution records.
Supply the common pattern of value, unit, method, observation time and ingestion time used by condition, area, occupancy and resource-performance findings.
Supply record validity bounds, real-world validity, change kind and supersession semantics applied uniformly across facility findings.

Align facility identity, composition and placement with the IFC spatial structure. Alignment only: IFC subordinates IfcBuilding to IfcFacility by subtyping, whereas this model aggregates buildings under a facility.
Align geometry, level of detail and city-object versioning for geospatial exchange and digital-twin use, independent of GML or any other encoding.
Align facility handover content with the Facility, Level, Space, Zone, Type, Component, System, Job and Document tables so construction-to-operations exchange is lossless in the covered subset.
Align persistent identifiers, lifespan versioning and construction-condition semantics for European geospatial publication.

Align to linked-data building vocabularies for graph projection. Recorded as partial: neither vocabulary offers a facility class between site and building, so facility identity must be carried by an extension term.
Align the facility asset register, criticality, life-cycle decision-making and documented-information requirements with the asset management system that governs the portfolio.
Align information requirements, trigger events and asset information model acceptance with the operational-phase information management process.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the same EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard PDF is dated 2014-10-01 Version 2 by claude (SRC-004) and 2006-01-06 Version 2.0 by grok (SRC-003), and the two providers assign it different authority tiers. Re-fetch and pin one date, version and tier before any citation is published.

Pin a single IFC documentation reference: claude cites the ifc43-docs build 4.3.2.20260821 (IFC4X3_ADD2) while grok cites standards.buildingsmart.org IFC 4.3.2.0 mapped to ISO 16739-1:2024. Both URLs must be re-resolved live and one canonical citation chosen for IfcFacility, IfcFacilityPart and IfcSite.

All ISO sources on both sides (41011, 6707-4, 19650-3, 55001, 81346-12, 15686-1) were taken from catalogue or Online Browsing Platform records, not normative clause text. Hold any clause-level or conformance wording; publish alignment language only, and state the non-reading explicitly in the draft.

Claude records that the FY2026 FRPP Data Dictionary and the EPA FIDS PDF could not be machine-parsed, so element names, formats and code values are unverified. Publish these as existence-and-authority citations only; block implementation-level field naming until re-parsed.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete. The merged evidence is dominated by US federal instruments (FRS, FRPP, NARA GRS 5.4, ISC, IBC, ENERGY STAR, ECHO) plus EU INSPIRE and one healthcare alignment. Validate against at least one non-US built-asset profile and one non-building civil or infrastructure profile before presenting the model as domain-general.

The five accepted grok findings each rest on a narrower evidence base than the base findings around them (IFC property sets for life safety, a single ECHO dictionary for compliance status, one IBC section for occupancy authorization). Mark them as provisionally sourced in the draft and re-verify before they carry any normative weight.

model.name: Site / Campus
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, describe, govern and operate a site or campus: a bounded area of land (with associated subsurface, surface water and airspace) held under coordinated management control, inside which facilities, infrastructure, circulation and open space are operated as one unit.
model.scope_statement: WM-BLT-008 models the managed physical container itself - its identity, classification, spatial extent, composition, control, lifecycle, operating conditions, measurement boundary and evidence - and stops at the interfaces with contained facilities (WM-BLT-006), the containing settlement or place (WM-PLC-005 / WM-PLC-002), the legal land unit, and the parties that own or operate it. Facilities, parcels, organisations, permits and individual assets are referenced by identifier, never re-modelled here. The model is projection-independent: IFC, CityGML, GeoJSON, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings of these semantics, not the semantics.
in_scope: Site identity, naming, coding and identifier crosswalks across authoritative registries and internal systems
Site typology and classification against governed schemes
Declared managed extent: what is inside the site, including discontiguous parts and third-party enclaves
Boundary geometry, coordinate reference system, elevation datum, vertical and subsurface extent
References to the land parcels and tenure instruments the site rests on
Containment of facilities (WM-BLT-006) and on-site infrastructure networks
Ground surface, landscape, open space, parking and laydown areas
Internal zones, precincts, development phases, circulation routes and control points
Ownership, operatorship, duty-holder accountability and delegation
Regulatory authorisations, permits and registry interests attached to the site
Physical access control, perimeter and site information sensitivity
Lifecycle states, boundary change events, split/merge and successor lineage
Operating hours, site rules, permit-to-work regimes and service provision
Natural hazard exposure, contamination and environmental constraints
Emergency preparedness, evacuation and muster arrangements
Site-level quantities, areas, occupancy and capacity
Energy, water, waste and greenhouse-gas reporting boundary and meter coverage
Site-scale monitoring platforms and observations
Site records, evidence, provenance and retention
Alignment and crosswalks to external schemas and operational systems
out_of_scope: Internal anatomy of a building or civil facility - storeys, spaces, rooms, systems and building elements (WM-BLT-006 and its children)
Legal land title, deeds, rights, restrictions and responsibilities as first-class legal objects (land administration sibling model, aligned to ISO 19152-1)
Settlement, administrative area and populated-place semantics (WM-PLC-005, WM-PLC-002)
Legal entity, organisation and person records for owners, operators, staff, visitors and contractors
Individual equipment and plant items, their maintenance history and work orders (asset register and maintenance sibling models)
Construction and capital project delivery processes, programmes and contracts
Lease, licence and other commercial agreement terms
Address and geocoding conceptual model - addresses are referenced, not defined here
Utility network topology, capacity modelling and operations beyond the site demarcation point
Sensor and actuator device specifications - observations are referenced through SOSA/SSN patterns
Environmental permit legal instruments as documents of record (authorisation sibling model)
Financial valuation, depreciation and real-estate investment accounting

boundary_notes.distinction: IFC 4.3 keeps IfcSite and IfcFacility as separate spatial structure elements: a facility is aggregated by IfcProject, IfcSite or another IfcFacility, and decomposes into IfcFacilityPart and IfcSpace. WM-BLT-008 therefore records the containment edge, the facility identifier and the site-side demarcation point, and never re-states facility-internal structure.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Land parcel / cadastral parcel (land administration sibling model)
boundary_notes.distinction: A cadastral parcel is a legal spatial unit with homogeneous property rights, identified by nationalCadastralReference and inspireId, and used primarily as a locator. A site is a management construct: it may span many parcels, occupy part of a parcel, or include parcels held under different tenure. IFC 4.3 deprecated IfcSite.LandTitleNumber, reinforcing that title belongs elsewhere. WM-BLT-008 references parcels; it does not model rights, restrictions or responsibilities.

A settlement is an administrative or populated-place concept; a site is an operational container under a single management regime. A site can straddle two settlements or lie wholly outside any populated place, so containment by settlement is a recorded relationship with its own evidence, not a derived truth.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Regulatory facility registry entries (e.g. EPA FRS facility site)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA FRS clusters program-system records under a 12-digit Registry ID and treats the originating programs as source of truth. A regulatory facility site is a reporting unit that frequently does not align one-to-one with the managed site: one site may carry several FRS interests, and one FRS record may cover only part of a site. The crosswalk must be recorded with match confidence rather than assumed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reporting boundary constructs (ENERGY STAR property, GHG Protocol organizational boundary)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA Portfolio Manager models a campus as a parent property with child properties and does not support nested campuses; GHG Protocol sets organizational boundaries by equity share or control. Both are accounting boundaries that can diverge from the physical managed extent. WM-BLT-008 records each reporting boundary as a distinct, dated view over the site, never as the site's definition.

On-site distribution is in scope only up to the demarcation point where responsibility passes to an external network operator. Network topology, hydraulic or electrical modelling and upstream operations sit in the utility network sibling model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Asset management system (ISO 55001) and asset information model (ISO 19650)
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 55001 governs the management system and ISO 19650 governs information containers and trigger events. WM-BLT-008 is neither: it is the subject those systems act upon. It records which management system and information requirements apply, and cites their identifiers, without absorbing their clauses.

selectedFindings.name: Site identity, identifier priority and designation
selectedFindings.description: How a site instance is uniquely identified and named across authoritative registries and internal systems, which identifier is canonical, and how identifiers may be retired.

selectedFindings.name: Site boundary geometry, spatial referencing and vertical extent
selectedFindings.description: The geometric representation of the site's extent, the coordinate reference system and datums that make it interpretable, its positional accuracy and provenance, and how far it reaches above and below ground.

selectedFindings.name: External context, addresses and connection points
selectedFindings.description: How the site meets the outside world: public access points, postal and emergency addresses, utility demarcation points and adjacency to neighbouring land uses.

selectedFindings.name: Contained facilities and containment semantics
selectedFindings.description: Which facilities the site contains, what containment means for each, and where the site record hands over to the facility record.

selectedFindings.name: Ground, landscape and open space
selectedFindings.description: The surface condition of the site between and around facilities: land cover, landscape and ecology, parking, laydown and unbuilt reserve.

selectedFindings.name: Ownership, operatorship and accountability
selectedFindings.description: Distinguishing the legal owner, the operator, the duty holder and delegated site management roles, each with scope and effective dates.

selectedFindings.name: Perimeter, physical access authorisation and logging
selectedFindings.description: How the site perimeter is defined and defended, how entry authorisations are granted and enforced at defined entry and exit points, and what access records are kept.

selectedFindings.name: Lifecycle states, transitions and boundary change lineage
selectedFindings.description: The controlled vocabulary of site states, the authority and evidence needed to transition between them, and how splits, merges and boundary changes preserve traceable lineage with separate event and record times.

selectedFindings.name: Operating model, hours, site rules and services
selectedFindings.description: The regime under which the site runs: operating periods, mandatory site rules and inductions, permit-to-work controls, and the services provided to occupants and how they are sourced.

selectedFindings.name: Site quantities, areas, occupancy and capacity
selectedFindings.description: The measured quantities that describe the site, each with a declared measurement basis, unit, method and date, distinguishing land area from aggregated floor area and design capacity from actual occupancy.

composition.purpose: Site / Campus specialises the generic place concept, inheriting spatial referencing and naming semantics while adding managed-container behaviour.
Records the settlement or populated place that spatially contains the site, as an evidenced relationship rather than a derived truth, since a site may straddle or fall outside settlement boundaries.
The site aggregates facility records; IFC 4.3 confirms a facility may be aggregated by a site and that facility-internal structure belongs to the facility.

composition.target: Land administration / property right sibling model (LADM-aligned)
composition.purpose: Supplies parcels, basic administrative units, parties and rights, responsibilities and restrictions that the site references but must not re-model.
Resolves owner, operator, duty holder, service provider and regulator references; site identity must never be conflated with the operating legal entity.
Supplies typed addresses for postal, delivery, emergency and registered purposes; IFC deprecated the site-embedded address attribute, reinforcing external ownership of addressing.

composition.target: Authorisation, permit and licence sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds permits, licences and consents as legal instruments; the site records only which authorisations apply, their validity and their operational conditions.

composition.target: Asset register and maintenance sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds individual plant and equipment items and their work history; the site provides the location and management context under ISO 55001 rather than the asset records themselves.
Owns external network topology and operations; the site records only on-site distribution and the demarcation point where responsibility transfers.
Supplies Platform, Sensor, Observation, FeatureOfInterest and the normative separation of phenomenon time from result time, reused rather than redefined by this model.
Supplies the versioned-object pattern with beginLifespanVersion and endLifespanVersion alongside real-world validFrom and validTo, keeping event time and record time distinct.
Alignment target for spatial structure, composition type and site reference geometry. Alignment only: LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress are deprecated in IFC 4.3 and are not carried forward.
Alignment target for encoding-independent geospatial representation, city object grouping, land use and relief at site scale.
Alignment target for parcel referencing and lifespan versioning attributes when operating in the European regulatory context.
Alignment target for management-system scope, accountability, life-cycle planning and control of change applied to the site as a managed object.
Alignment target for information containers, suitability status, the common data environment as agreed source of information, and the trigger-event update pattern.

composition.target: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard boundary rules
composition.purpose: Alignment target for organizational and operational boundary setting when a site emissions inventory is compiled.

Alignment target for regulatory site identification and crosswalk reconciliation in the United States context; the FRS Registry ID is a master-system identifier candidate, not a global site identifier.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the two providers cite IFC 4.3 from different hosts (ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org versus standards.buildingsmart.org) and different documentation builds, and grok-sourced Pset_SiteCommon, Pset_LandRegistration and IfcMapConversion claims must be re-fetched and pinned against the single host and version chosen for the base before merge.

Paywalled and blocked sources remain unverified at clause level: ISO catalogue entries (55001, 19650-1, 19650-3, 19152-1, 19152-2, 41011, 6707-1), IEC 62264-1 and the ENERGY STAR campus guide PDF were cited for title, edition and scope only; no clause-level wording may be published as quotation or requirement.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete: the synthesised model must be exercised against at least three materially different site profiles (for example a university or hospital campus, a process or industrial site, and a port, data-centre or utility holding) before publication, since the evidence pack contains no instance-level validation.

Jurisdictional profile verification is outstanding: emergency planning (29 CFR 1910.38), regulatory site identity (EPA FRS), benchmarking (ENERGY STAR), physical security (NIST SP 800-53), contaminated land (CERCLA/RCRA) and construction wage envelopes (29 CFR 5.2) are all United States instruments; at least one non-US jurisdiction cross-check is required before the model is presented as jurisdiction-neutral.

No governed global location identifier scheme is asserted: GS1 GLN could not be fetched (HTTP 403) and ISO/IEC 81346 reference designation texts are paywalled, so any identifier-grammar claim must stay out of the published draft.

model.name: Building / Structure
model.purpose: Represent a persistent building or engineered structure as a governed physical artifact with identity, geometry, composition, fabric, materials, systems, capabilities, condition, performance and lifecycle evidence independent of any storage or exchange format.
model.scope_statement: Owns built-artifact identity, class, geometry bindings, spatial and fabric decomposition, material and installed-system bindings, measured physical properties, recognition features, affordances, hazards, condition and performance assessments, lifecycle changes and exchange projections while referencing facility, site, space, equipment, works, party, permit, incident and document masters.
in_scope: Building and engineered-structure identity, classification, recognition, geometry, pose and spatial decomposition
Structural system, envelope, materials, physical properties, installed-system bindings, capabilities, affordances and hazards
Condition, performance, design and as-built provenance, alteration, end of life, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Facility operations, land and site tenure, postal address authority, room occupancy and tenancy, individual equipment and product master lifecycles
Construction-project and work-order execution, party identity, permits, incidents, finance, valuation, insurance and document payloads
Universal building-code, safety, load, energy, condition or structure-subtype vocabularies

boundary_notes.distinction: Building or structure owns physical fabric; Facility owns the managed operational aggregation. A facility may contain buildings even though IFC uses a different type hierarchy.
The artifact references location, cadastral and address authorities but does not own land tenure, site management or address normalization.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Premises, space and spatial unit WM-BLT-002
boundary_notes.distinction: This model owns the outer artifact and decomposition bindings; independently usable or governed interior units retain their own identity and lifecycle.
The structure owns serving-system, interface and scope bindings while equipment serial identity, maintenance, warranty and spare-parts lifecycle stay external.
Works create or alter the artifact, but schedules, contracts, resources, cost and execution remain in project and work models; accepted outputs update the physical record.
An incident occurs externally, a defect or damage observation is recorded here, an engineering assessment interprets it, and repair execution remains a referenced work record.

selectedFindings.name: Authoritative identity, namespace and version
selectedFindings.description: Master-system identifier, namespace, immutable revision and record authority for the physical artifact.

selectedFindings.name: Site, parcel, address and geographic references
selectedFindings.description: Typed external location references with jurisdiction and master authority, without importing tenure or address lifecycle.

selectedFindings.name: Premises, space, zone and containment boundary
selectedFindings.description: References to interior units and functional zones plus the boundary or rule by which elements are contained.

selectedFindings.name: Load path, actions, capacity and design basis
selectedFindings.description: Declared design actions, combinations, load transfer, resistance, serviceability and code or engineering basis without asserting current safety.

selectedFindings.name: System identity, function, scope and topology
selectedFindings.description: References to systems and components with served areas, ports, networks, function and operational boundary.

selectedFindings.name: Capacity, availability, control and dependency
selectedFindings.description: Rated and observed capacity, service state, control authority, utilities, upstream dependencies and failure propagation.

selectedFindings.name: Supported use, occupancy, load, access and egress
selectedFindings.description: Permitted or designed uses, occupancy and load limits, accessibility, circulation, entry, exit and evacuation affordances.

selectedFindings.name: Inspection method, scope, access and limitations
selectedFindings.description: Inspector, competence, method, covered and inaccessible parts, instruments, conditions, time, evidence and limitations.

selectedFindings.name: Owner, operator, custodian and record authority
selectedFindings.description: Time-bounded external party roles and distinct authority over fabric, operation, data and decisions.

composition.purpose: Binds operational aggregation while the building retains independent physical identity and fabric lifecycle.
Provides the candidate spatial matryoshka for independently governed interior units while preserving their typed identities.

composition.target: Site, Land Parcel, Address and Geography models
composition.purpose: Locates the physical artifact without importing cadastral, tenure or address mastership.
Binds installed components and material classifications while external masters own serial, product and supply lifecycles.

composition.target: Construction Works, Project and Work Order models
composition.purpose: Links creation and alteration evidence while execution remains independently governed.

composition.target: Person, Organization, Ownership, Permit and Document models
composition.purpose: Binds parties, interests, authorizations and evidence without absorbing their lifecycle.
Links damaging events and external hazards while storing only building-local observations and assessments.

model.name: Gazetteer Place
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an AI agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate a governed gazetteer place record: a named real-world location identified by a geographic identifier, with temporally scoped toponyms, classification, position, authority, provenance, relationships and access controls.
model.scope_statement: The model covers one place as recorded in a gazetteer, i.e. an ISO 19112 location instance identified by a geographic identifier within a declared location type and gazetteer register. It covers naming (multilingual, multi-script, temporally scoped), place-type classification, representative position and geometry with declared CRS and accuracy, existence and record lifecycle, naming authority and decisions, provenance and attestation, hierarchy and topology, cross-gazetteer concordance, sensitivity and access control, validation and retention. It excludes address semantics, coordinate reference system definition, boundary determination, cartographic rendering and any observation that merely cites a place.
in_scope: Place record identity, identifier minting, persistence and resolution
Toponyms with language, script, transliteration, pronunciation, nativeness, status and temporal validity
Place type / feature type classification including local types and type change over time
Representative position, geometry set, extent, CRS declaration and coordinate encoding constraints
Positional accuracy, resolution, viewing-scale bounds and fitness-for-use statements
Real-world existence period and record version lifespan, including uncertain and open-ended dates
Supersession, merge, split, deprecation and tombstoning of place records
Naming authority scope, official status, decision process and effective dates
Contested, disputed and competing names or claims and their audience-scoped presentation
Custodian, administrator, contributor, licence and editorial lineage
Partitive/administrative hierarchy and topological or associative relations to other places
Concordance to external gazetteers with match type and confidence
Sensitivity classification, locality generalization and access rules
Validation, conformance testing and quality measurement
Exchange encodings and query-service projections as non-semantic renderings
out_of_scope: Address and addressable-object semantics (ISO 19160-1 address model, address components, postal templates)
Definition of coordinate reference systems, datums and transformations (ISO 19111 / EPSG registry content)
Legal determination or delimitation of administrative and international boundaries
Cadastral parcels, property rights and land tenure
Building, facility and asset management records
Commercial point-of-interest operations such as opening hours, capacity, booking and pricing
Transport network topology, route segments and navigation instructions
Cartographic styling, symbolisation and map production
Observation, occurrence, event or transaction records that merely reference a place
Language, script, country and currency code registries themselves

boundary_notes.distinction: A gazetteer place is a named real-world feature referenced indirectly by a geographic identifier; an address is a structured, human-oriented designation of an addressable object. ISO/TC 211 concluded that addressing requirements are sufficiently different from the scope of ISO 19112, so address components must be referenced, not absorbed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Administrative unit and statistical geography registers (UN M49, ISO 3166, INSPIRE AU)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a place sits in, or is coded to, an administrative or statistical area and carries country codes; it does not define the area hierarchy, its legal basis or its boundary geometry, which remain owned by the register. UN M49 explicitly disclaims political interpretation of its groupings.

The place record declares which CRS its coordinates are expressed in and how they are encoded; the definition of the CRS, its datum and its transformations is external. GeoSPARQL 1.1 treats spatial reference system as a broader category than CRS and relies on external CRS identity in geometry literals.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Point-of-interest / local business model (schema.org Place and LocalBusiness)
boundary_notes.distinction: schema.org Place mixes stable physical extension with operational commerce attributes such as opening hours, capacity and booking pages. Only the stable named-place core is in scope; operational and commercial attributes belong to a sibling POI/venue model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Place type / feature type vocabulary (GeoNames feature classes and codes, Getty AAT, INSPIRE NamedPlaceTypeValue)
boundary_notes.distinction: The model requires a classification assertion with a resolvable vocabulary concept and optional source label, but the controlled vocabulary itself is a separate classifier model with its own versioning and deprecation rules.

Attestations, citations and name sources are first-class here as links plus temporal and confidence qualifiers, but the bibliographic description of the cited work (authors, edition, holdings) is delegated to a citation model.

selectedFindings.name: Place record identity and identifier minting
selectedFindings.description: A gazetteer place is identified by a persistent, opaque identifier that survives renaming, reclassification and geometry revision. Authoritative master-system identifiers (GNIS Feature ID, INSPIRE inspireId, national gazetteer key) take precedence; a governed HTTP URI is minted for web resolution; only where no external authority exists does the adopting Dimension mint a UUID or ULID. A date, a name or a coordinate pair is never the identifier.

selectedFindings.name: Geographic identifier, location type and indirect spatial referencing
selectedFindings.description: ISO 19112 positions a gazetteer as a directory of geographic identifiers describing location instances, where a location type defines the semantics of the instances it admits. The place record must therefore declare which gazetteer register and which location type it belongs to, and must support indirect referencing — resolving a label or code to a position rather than carrying coordinates alone.

selectedFindings.name: Representative position and multiple geometries
selectedFindings.description: A place may carry a representative point, a bounding box, one or more detailed geometries, or no geometry at all. GeoSPARQL distinguishes hasGeometry from hasDefaultGeometry and provides derived centroid and area; LPF permits several temporally scoped geometries with per-geometry certainty and citations, or a null geometry; Getty TGN records point and bounding-box coordinates.

selectedFindings.name: Sensitivity classification, generalization and disclosure
selectedFindings.description: GBIF defines graded sensitivity categories with matching coordinate generalization (region only, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 degrees), prefers grid-based generalization over randomization, requires that withholding and generalization be disclosed in dedicated fields, places the sensitivity decision with the data provider, and requires a recorded date for reviewing the sensitivity status. The same pattern governs culturally restricted, security-sensitive and privacy-sensitive places.

composition.target: Gazetteer register and location type registry (ISO 19112 gazetteer / location type)
composition.purpose: Every place record must declare the gazetteer that publishes it and the location type whose definition it satisfies; the register and type definitions are governed separately from individual instances.

composition.target: Address and addressable-object model (ISO 19160-1 conceptual model)
composition.purpose: Link a place to addresses that designate it without importing address component or postal-template semantics, which ISO/TC 211 treats as a distinct scope from geographic identifiers.

composition.target: Country and area code registry (ISO 3166-1 and UN M49)
composition.purpose: Supply the country or area codes that contextualise the place; LPF makes country codes a required property and the register carries the disclaimer about legal status and frontiers.

composition.target: Administrative and statistical area model (INSPIRE Administrative Units, national admin hierarchies)
composition.purpose: Provide the parent administrative and statistical units that a place belongs to, without duplicating their legal basis, boundary geometry or versioning.

composition.target: Coordinate reference system model (ISO 19111 / EPSG-style register)
composition.purpose: Resolve the CRS identifiers declared on geometries and support transformation provenance; CRS definitions are external and must not be restated here.

composition.target: Language, script and transliteration registries (ISO 639, ISO 15924, romanization systems)
composition.purpose: Validate the language, script and transliteration-scheme values on every name spelling, as required by the INSPIRE GeographicalName structure.

composition.target: Place type vocabulary / feature classifier model (GeoNames feature codes, Getty AAT place types, INSPIRE code lists)
composition.purpose: Supply resolvable place-type concepts and their versioning and deprecation rules; the place record holds only the classification assertion and its source label.
Compose the place with zero or more geometries carrying role, CRS, temporal scope, certainty and serialisation, following the GeoSPARQL separation of feature from geometry.
Attach per-assertion citations with locus, date and confidence to names, types, geometries and relations, as LPF and INSPIRE sourceOfName require.

composition.target: Agent and organisation model (authorities, custodians, contributors)
composition.purpose: Identify naming authorities, gazetteer custodians, instance administrators and contributors as governed agents rather than free-text strings.

composition.target: Temporal period vocabulary model (named historical periods)
composition.purpose: Resolve named period concepts used to scope existence, names and geometries where calendar dates are unavailable or inappropriate.
Carry licence, attribution and inherited source restrictions on the record and on derived representations.
Alignment target for NamedPlace, GeographicalName, SpellingOfName and lifespan versioning; alignment is asserted at element level and does not by itself constitute a conformance claim.
Alignment target for temporally scoped names, types, geometries, relations and typed links, and for the required title, country codes and feature classes.

composition.target: OGC GeoSPARQL 1.1 Feature and Geometry ontology
composition.purpose: Alignment target for feature-geometry structure, serialisations and topological relation families when the record is projected to RDF.
Alignment target for the query-service projection: item addressing, bbox and datetime parameters, default CRS and link relations.

composition.target: Point-of-interest and venue model (schema.org Place / LocalBusiness operational attributes)
composition.purpose: Alignment for web discoverability of the stable named-place core while explicitly excluding operational and commercial attributes.

composition.target: Sensitive-data handling policy model (graded generalization and disclosure)
composition.purpose: Apply graded sensitivity categories, generalization magnitudes, disclosure fields and review dates to any place whose precise location can cause harm.

publicationHolds: ISO 19112:2019 normative text was reached by neither provider (ISO catalogue returned HTTP 403 for one, paywalled for the other). Class names, attribute names, cardinalities and the 2003-to-2019 rename set are unverified, and the two providers report different vocabularies for the same construct. Verify against the purchased standard or the ISO/TC 211 register before publishing any wording that a reader could mistake for a conformance statement.

Live-URL and version-pin verification for every accepted source. Specifically: the US BGN Principles, Policies and Procedures edition date was not machine-extractable; the INSPIRE Geographical Names Technical Guidelines are cited by the two providers as a versioned PDF (v3.1.0, 2024-07-31) and as a knowledge-base landing page and must be reconciled to one pinned artifact; and the three grok-sourced additions carry only tier-2 or accessed-page evidence.

Multi-profile domain validation is incomplete. The model is exercised only against US BGN/GNIS, INSPIRE/EU regulatory practice and compiled gazetteers (GeoNames, Getty TGN, Who's On First, Linked Places Format). Run it against at least one non-US, non-EU national names authority and one historical or linked-pasts gazetteer profile before publication, and re-test the ISO 19112 descriptive-position case against INSPIRE's mandatory NamedPlace geometry to confirm the optional-geometry-with-absence-reason resolution holds in both profiles.

Indigenous and culturally restricted place-name governance is a gap the base declares and the accepted grok finding only partially fills. No Indigenous data-sovereignty instrument (CARE Principles, UNDRIP as applied to toponyms) was examined by either provider. Do not present the sensitivity and access layer as canonical, and mark the community-warrant question as provisional.

Temporal-uncertainty syntax is ungrounded: the intended EDTF (ISO 8601-2) grounding failed with HTTP 403, leaving approximate, uncertain and unspecified-digit dates supported only by the Linked Places 'when' object. Publish no specific uncertainty syntax.

Sensitivity categories and their thresholds derive from a biodiversity-occurrence context expressed in decimal degrees, and no national security-classification regime was consulted, so the mapping from sensitivity category to government classification level is undefined and the thresholds are unvalidated at high latitudes and for cultural restriction.
